replication.target_description: Probe negative priming: age-specific animal RT contrast unresolved; no current building condition.

notes: Identity assessment: supplied candidate is an HTML transcription of the primary Brief Report, not the hosting site's AI summary. Article title, Emmanuel Ahr/Olivier Houdé/Grégoire Borst authorship, Journal of Experimental Child Psychology 145 (2016) 157–165, and school-aged negative-priming design match the supplied replication reference. The DOI itself is hidden as [Link] in this transcription, so DOI identity is not directly verified. Methods, Results, Discussion and References are reproduced with overlapping segments; no target PDF was supplied, so original PDF layout and the g2p glyph cannot be checked. Original paper is outside assigned scope; original and unassigned fields are placeholders only. The three assigned probe rows have identical descriptions and p.6 locator (journal p.162), without specifying grade, same/different animal probes, or a building condition. Current paper uses animal probes only; buildings are discussed as a condition in the previous adult paper. Matching printed d candidates for identical-animal RT negative priming: 1st grade t(31) = 2.27, p < .05, d = 0.20; 3rd grade t(22) = 2.43, p < .05, d = 0.20; 5th grade t(25) = 4.08, p < .001, d = .37. Final participant group candidates are respectively 31, 22, 25, explicitly given in Participants; these were not inferred from the t degrees of freedom, whose printed labels are retained. Different-animal control tests are t(27) = 1.26, p = .22; t(20) = 1.02, p = .32; t(23) = 2.07, p = .051, with no d printed in that paragraph. Aggregate probe RT main effect is F(1, 75) = 22.00, p < .001, g2p = .23; type-of-prime by animal-probe interaction is F(1, 67) = 6.24, p < .05, g2p = .09. These are distinct tests and are not substitutes for the grade-specific d tests. No candidate was assigned by audit ID, row order, or numeric matching. N = 78 (31 + 22 + 25) is the final overall participant sample, not an automatically applicable grade-specific test N. Children with chance performance were excluded; RT trial exclusions were 2.5%, 3.1%, 4.0% by grade.
